title: Principal quotient-completion model with its normalized unit
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $t$ a global section of $R$. Use $D(\mathcal A)$ and its localization $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a complex $P$, let $U(P)$ be the strict tower $((R/t^{n+1}R)[0]\otimes_R P)_{n\geq0}$ with the existing quotient transitions and maps $q_n:P\to U(P)_n$ [def-pur-principal-koszul-quotient-towers]. Define these towers functorially on complexes, and put $G(P)=\mathsf C(U(P))$, the actual shifted Roos cone [def-weil-strict-roos-model]. A principal quotient-completion model is a functor $C:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$, a counit $c:C\circ Q\Rightarrow Q\circ G$ making $C$ the total left derived functor of $Q\circ G$ at quasi-isomorphisms, and the property that $c_P$ is invertible for every K-flat $P$ [def-pc-kflat-complex]. It also includes a natural unit $\eta:1\Rightarrow C$ and maps $b_P:P\to G(P)$ whose canonical Roos coordinates in degree $p+1$ are $(0,(q_n^{p+1})_n)$, with $c_P\circ\eta_{QP}=Q(b_P)$ for every complex $P$. The universal condition means that composing with $c$ gives a bijection between natural transformations $H\Rightarrow C$ and $H\circ Q\Rightarrow Q\circ G$ for every $H:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$. This defines the model data and its normalization, without asserting existence or choosing data from a mere existence theorem.
